(frog-mirror)=
# frog-mirror

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-success}`Geometry` Write the mirror image (enantiomer) of every structure in an ensemble.

## What it does

Enantiomers (mirror-image molecules) have exactly the same energy and the same achiral
properties, so you only need to compute one of them. When you need the other — to build the
opposite enantiomer of a catalyst, to get the second hand of a racemic conformer search, or to
compare a computed ECD spectrum with the measured one (the mirror image has the opposite ECD
sign) — this command writes it instantly, without recomputing anything.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-mirror/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

Any geometry: an `.xyz` file (all structures of a multi-XYZ, e.g. `crest_conformers.xyz`, are
mirrored) or an ORCA/Gaussian output (its last geometry). No calculation keyword is needed.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | XYZ, ORCA or Gaussian file(s) |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| File | `<stem>_mirror.xyz` | always | Mirrored structures in XYZ format, in input order |

### How to read it

No table: one XYZ file per input, with the structures in the same order and the original comment
lines (e.g. CREST energies) copied unchanged. Atom order is unchanged too, so atom numbers stay
valid for other commands.

* The x coordinate of every atom is inverted (reflection through the yz plane): the molecule may
  appear flipped in the viewer, which is expected.
* Example: `nmr_iPr.xyz` has C0 = S and C2 = R; `nmr_iPr_mirror.xyz` has C0 = R and C2 = S.
* Mirroring an **achiral** molecule (or a meso compound) gives the same molecule again.
* Molecules with axial, helical or planar chirality (atropisomers, helicenes, planar-chiral
  complexes) are mirrored correctly too, even though `frog-stereocenters` finds no R/S centre.

## Step by step

1. Run `frog-mirror crest_conformers.xyz`: it writes `crest_conformers_mirror.xyz` next to the input (use `--out-dir DIR` to put it elsewhere).
2. Optionally check the result with `frog-stereocenters crest_conformers_mirror.xyz`: every R centre should now be S and vice versa.
3. Use the mirrored structures as starting points of new calculations; their energies are the same as those of the originals, so a re-optimisation is only needed if you change method.

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-mirror --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-mirror --help`
```text
usage: frog-mirror [-h] [-v] [-q] [--out-dir DIR] file [file ...]

Write the mirror image (enantiomer) of every structure in an ensemble.

The x coordinate of every atom is inverted (reflection through the yz plane). Comment lines (e.g.
energies) are copied unchanged.

positional arguments:
  file           XYZ, ORCA or Gaussian file(s)

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit

output:
  -v, --verbose  Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet    Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --out-dir DIR  Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file)

outputs:
  files (next to each input, or --out-dir):
    <stem>_mirror.xyz           Mirrored structures in XYZ format, in input order

examples:
  frog-mirror crest_conformers.xyz
      Write crest_conformers_mirror.xyz next to the input
  frog-mirror opt_R.out --out-dir enantiomer
      Write enantiomer/opt_R_mirror.xyz

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-mirror.md.
```
:::
